faq.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Short answers about the new Nostr-only Obelisk.

q1.question: What is Obelisk?
q1.answer: Obelisk is an open-source, Discord-style group chat client that runs entirely on Nostr. There is no backend and no database: every message is a signed Nostr event published directly to the relays you choose. Groups are NIP-29 groups, DMs are encrypted Nostr DMs, and your account is a Nostr keypair.

q2.question: Is there a server I have to sign up to?
q2.answer: No. Obelisk is a frontend. There is no signup, no email, no password, and no Obelisk account. You log in with a Nostr key and the app talks straight to your configured relays: there is no Obelisk application backend or database. Messages live on relays. Obelisk operates two public relays; every other relay is controlled by its own operator.

q3.question: What relays does Obelisk use?
q3.answer: Whatever relays you tell it to. New installs currently include wss://public.obelisk.ar and wss://lacrypta-relay.obelisk.ar, both operated by Obelisk. You can add, remove, or replace relays from the relay rail. Every other relay is independent and controlled by its own operator.

q4.question: Do I need an email or phone number?
q4.answer: No. Obelisk has no signup form. You log in with a Nostr key: through a browser extension (NIP-07), through a signer app such as Amber or nsec.app over NIP-46 (scan a QR code or paste a bunker link), or by pasting an nsec. The login screen can also generate a new key for you.

q5.question: How are groups implemented?
q5.answer: Obelisk uses NIP-29: relay-managed groups. Channels, members, admins and removals are all standard NIP-29 events that the relay enforces. Any NIP-29-compatible relay works. You can host your own relay, run a private one for your community, or use a public one.

q6.question: Are my messages encrypted?
q6.answer: Direct messages are end-to-end encrypted. Obelisk sends NIP-17 gift-wrapped messages by default, so relays cannot see who you are talking to, and you can switch a conversation back to NIP-04 if the other person's client needs it. Post-quantum protection is on by default: whenever your signer and the other person both have post-quantum keys, the message is sealed with a post-quantum envelope as well (you can turn it off in settings). Group messages are signed but public on the relay: anyone the relay lets in can read them, just like a Discord channel. Run a private relay if you need a closed group.

q7.question: Can I self-host Obelisk?
q7.answer: Yes. Obelisk is a Next.js app with no database to manage and no backend service of its own: its small server part serves the pages, sets security headers, unfurls link previews and renders the public note and profile pages. Run it locally with `npm run dev`, ship it to any Node host with `npm run build` and `npm start`, or expose it through a tunnel. A static-export build for GitHub Pages, S3 or a static CDN is still on the roadmap.

q8.question: How do I get a Nostr key?
q8.answer: You can generate one in the login screen. If you want a standalone signer, install a NIP-07 browser extension like Alby or nos2x, or on mobile use Amber (Android) or nsec.app. Keep your nsec safe: it's your account, no one can recover it for you.

q9.question: What about voice channels?
q9.answer: Voice is here. Voice channels use WebRTC with signaling over Nostr events, so there is no Socket.io server and no Obelisk server in between. Small rooms connect browsers directly (a peer-to-peer mesh of up to four people); big-room voice channels route through a mediasoup SFU the channel admin picks, for many more people. Both do audio, camera and screen sharing.

q10.question: Does Obelisk work on mobile?
q10.answer: Yes. Obelisk is a responsive web app that works in any modern mobile browser, and you can install it to your home screen as a PWA from the browser menu, no app store needed. On a phone, log in with a signer app over NIP-46 (Amber, nsec.app), generate a new key, or paste an nsec.

q11.question: What does Obelisk keep on my device, and how do I remove it?
q11.answer: To open quickly and remember where you were, Obelisk keeps a copy of channels, messages and profiles, your read positions, your preferences, your login (encrypted) and the app's own files in your browser. None of it is sent to an Obelisk server: there is no account server, and what you publish lives on relays (the site does load Google Analytics, which counts visits with its own cookies). Remove any of it in Settings > Data on this device, or all of it with Remove everything from this device. You can also log out, clear the site data for obelisk.ar in your browser's settings, or use a private window, which keeps nothing once you close it. Clearing your device does not delete what you published: delete a message from its menu to send a deletion request (NIP-09), which each relay may or may not honour. Step by step: obelisk.ar/help/local-data.

features.heading: Why Obelisk
features.subtitle: All the chat. None of the servers. Your keys, your relays, signed events.

nostrIdentity.title: Nostr login: your keys, your account
nostrIdentity.desc: Sign in with a browser extension (NIP-07), a signer app over NIP-46, or your nsec. There is no Obelisk account to create. Your Nostr key is the account, everywhere.

realtimeChat.title: NIP-29 groups
realtimeChat.desc: Channels, members, admins and removals are all standard NIP-29 events on the relay. Open protocol, no proprietary format, no lock-in.

encryptedDMs.title: Encrypted DMs
encryptedDMs.desc: Direct messages are end-to-end encrypted Nostr DMs, gift-wrapped with NIP-17 by default and NIP-04 when a conversation needs it. Only you and the recipient can read them.

voice.title: P2P voice channels over Nostr
voice.desc: Talk to anyone in a channel with no media server in the middle. Voice is WebRTC peer-to-peer; signaling rides on Nostr events, just like every other message.

selfHosted.title: No backend, no database
selfHosted.desc: Obelisk is a frontend. There is no Postgres, no Socket.io server, no auth service. Every message is a signed event sent straight to a relay.

spamResistant.title: Simple self-hosting
spamResistant.desc: Self-hosting means running one Next.js app. No database to operate, no Docker required. Run it from your laptop, behind a tunnel, or on any Node host.

zaps.title: Bitcoin zaps in chat
zaps.desc: Send sats from any message via NIP-57 zaps, paid by a wallet you connect with Nostr Wallet Connect (NIP-47) or by a WebLN browser extension. No custodian, no platform fee, no middleman.

games.title: Games on the relay
games.desc: Chain Reaction, Vesta and Stacker run inside a channel with no game server. Every move is a signed event, and every client replays the same log to the same board.

adminCli.title: Open source
adminCli.desc: AGPL-3.0 licensed, every line on GitHub. Read it, fork it, audit it, run it. The whole app is the client you can see.

pqc.heading: Post-quantum messages
pqc.subtitle: Encrypted messages sent today can be recorded now and read years from now, once a quantum computer breaks the key exchange Nostr relies on. It is the one part of the problem that can be fixed in advance.
pqc.status: Live in Obelisk. Direct messages are gift-wrapped by default, and carry a post-quantum seal whenever post-quantum protection is on (it is by default) and your signer and the other person both have post-quantum keys. The keys themselves live in the Nostr WoT extension and the @nostr-wot/pq library.

nostrwot.desc: Identity, signer and post-quantum keys derived from a single 24-word recovery phrase.

quantakrypto.desc: Applied post-quantum cryptography: design, specification and cryptographic review.
